pr_title: backupccl: add privileges to SHOW BACKUP
pr_body:
Currently, restore resets the privileges on the descriptors that are
restored. This is because the backup may not have all the user/roles and
there may be conflicting user/roles even if it did. However, it is
useful to be able to retrieve the privileges assigned on descriptors in
a backup so that they can be recreated manually after the RESTORE.

Closes #45357.

Release note (enterprise change): The privileges assigned to a given
table/database are now visible through SHOW BACKUP. SHOW BACKUP will
list which users and roles had which privileges on each table/database
in the backup if the `WITH privileges` option is specified.
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/45862)

issue_context.title: backupccl: add option to show users and grants in SHOW BACKUP
issue_context.body: Unlike Full-Cluster backup/restore, per-table or per-database restore _do not_ preserve privileges on the restored tables as they cannot assume the users exist/are the same/etc. We currently advise operators to re-grant the correct users on the restoring cluster after restoring, but one pain point here is that they do no know what those grants should be -- the point of the backup was to record that kind of information. The backed up schema data for the tables in the backup _does_ include the grants and privileges so we can actually determine what the grants were, and including that in a version of SHOW BACKUP could at least allow an operator to then recreate those that they want, potentially remapping them as required to the correct users in the restoring cluster, by hand.

review_comments: Is there a SQL function that can pretty print privileges (maybe even as `GRANT`s? I wonder if we can reuse the logic from `dump`?
just curious: is it at all feasible to include them as `GRANT` statements in the `SCHEMAS` output instead?
